source_text:
Εἰς
μικρὸν εἶχε τὸ γῄδιον, ὦ ∆ιόνυσε, καὶ ταῖς ἐντεῦθεν ἐπανεῖχεν ἐλπίσι, τοῦτο μένων
λαβεῖν, ὃ ταῖς ἀμπέλοις ἐδόκει διδόναι· τί μὴ πολὺς ἐπελθὼν βριθούσας αὐτὰς
ἀπέδειξε τῷ καρπῷ; εἴθε καὶ ληνῶν ἐπέβης, καὶ βακχικὸν ἐπεχόρευσας, καὶ οὐδὲν
τοῦ γλεύκους ὑπῆρχε κενόν· ὅθεν ἔχων πλούτου καλῶς, ἐχόρευσεν ἂν ὑφ' ἡδονῆς
καὶ μουσικώτερος ἦν. Βούλει μαθεῖν καὶ ὅ τι πρὸς ταῦτά φησιν ὁ ∆ιόνυσος;
thought_title: Dionysus reproached for the poor man's small plot
orientation: Procopius is addressing Dionysus directly, complaining that the god did not make the poor man's vineyard rich.
pass_a_gloss: He had a small plot of land, O Dionysus, and he was holding on to the hopes from it, waiting to receive this, which it seemed right to give to the vines. Why did you not come in abundance and show them heavy with fruit? If only you had also set foot on the wine vats, and danced the Bacchic dance, and there was no part of the new wine empty. From which, having wealth nobly, he would have danced for pleasure and would have been more musical. Do you want to learn also what Dionysus says to these things?

choices.why: The diminutive form emphasizes the smallness of the land, matching the poor man's situation.

choices.english: was holding on to the hopes
choices.why: The verb ἐπανέχω with dative suggests clinging to or relying on the hopes, not merely having them.
ἀποδείκνυμι means to make something appear or display it; the accusative participle describes the vines as laden.
The adjective βακχικός refers to Bacchic rites; with ἐπιχορεύω it suggests performing the ritual dance upon the vats.

choices.english: there was no part of the new wine empty
choices.why: The partitive genitive with οὐδέν means no portion of the new wine was lacking or empty, i.e., the vats were full.
rejected: nothing of the new wine was empty
none of the new wine was lacking

choices.english: he would have danced for pleasure
choices.why: The potential optative with ἂν expresses what would have happened; ὑφ' ἡδονῆς indicates the cause, pleasure.
rejected: he would have danced from pleasure
he would have danced out of pleasure

pass_b_english: He had only a small plot of land, Dionysus, and he was holding on to the hopes that came from it, waiting to receive what the vines seemed ready to give. Why did you not come in abundance and show them heavy with fruit? If only you had stepped onto the wine vats and danced the Bacchic dance, and no part of the new wine had been left empty! From that he would have had wealth in fine measure, and he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical himself. Do you want to learn what Dionysus says to all this?

problems.quote: he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical
problems.source_quote: ἐχόρευσεν ἂν ὑφ' ἡδονῆς καὶ μουσικώτερος ἦν
problems.why: Subject is Dionysus (implied), not the poor man: 'you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical' — the god's presence brings music.
problems.fix: you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself
problems.ruling: ἐχόρευσεν ἂν with implied Dionysus subject; 'he' wrongly refers to the poor man, changing who dances.

edits.old: he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical
edits.new: you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself

fixed: Changed 'he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical' to 'you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself' to reflect that Dionysus is the implied subject.

problems.quote: you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself
problems.source_quote: ἐχόρευσεν ἂν ὑφ' ἡδονῆς καὶ μουσικώτερος ἦν
problems.why: Subject flipped: source says 'he' (the poor man) would have danced and been more musical, not Dionysus.
problems.fix: he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical himself.

edits.old: you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself
edits.new: he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical himself

fixed: Changed 'you would have danced for pleasure and been more musical yourself' to 'he would have danced for pleasure and been more musical himself' to restore the source's subject (the poor man).

last_rejected.quote: no part of the new wine had been left empty
last_rejected.why: 'ὑπῆρχε κενόν' means 'was empty/left empty', but 'no part...had been left empty' implies fullness; the Greek wishes nothing was empty, i.e., everything was full.
last_rejected.fix: and nothing of the new wine had stood empty
last_rejected.ruling: Greek 'οὐδὲν...ὑπῆρχε κενόν' = 'nothing was empty'; English 'no part...left empty' matches exactly. Claim misreads English.
